Mark Plays Nuitai

A blind playtest of the pygame demo by Mark, an invented professional playtester, thinking out loud. His notes follow the episode.

Mark Hi everyone, welcome back. Last time a burning Hina fell with the Noni Pulu refused, and the game ended with nothing saved, again. So: a fresh New Game. This time I want to find a save point before anything else, put a Kukui and Noni Pulu in both battle bags, and look for the hunters' lodge. I'm also going to pay attention to what past me wrote down about the opening.

Mark Title screen. Continue is gray, so there is nothing to continue; New Game it is, and I am keeping my fingers off z on the title this time, because last time that is how I started a game I did not mean to start. Four cards first. "In a world covered by endless water, people live on scattered islands, venturing across the ocean at their own peril." Then the sea monsters and storms, "miracles and oddities are daily routine", the cook and the priestess, and "Kulāiwi Village. The last day of Summer." I know all of this by heart now and it still sets the tone well. Short cards, one idea each, no wall of lore.

Mark Kailo, in the red headband, outside the two houses with the hens. "Stew for the wake tonight... cakes and breadfruit for the next island. If I leave now I'll be back before Melia's done her chores." Old Pono's wake is tonight. And here comes Melia, "Kailo! KAILO!", and the three boars in the taro patch, "That patch feeds three houses!" Hina walks up with "Then stop shouting and do something about it." I love Hina in this opening. One line and you know her.

Mark Melia wants to come along, "Let me fight with you." Kailo says it is too dangerous, "put that thing away before you break something", and she gets the gulls and the stew. Little sister, I said that last time, and "Aww." confirms it. A preemptive strike on the first boar, so the fight starts with free turns, which is a nice little reward for punching first.

Mark This is the tutorial fight. I know the rules, so I am going to play it the way I would play any fight: Light, then Medium, then Strong to build mana, Sauté for fire damage, and keep Hina healthy. Hina asked me if I remember how to fight and I said No again, mostly to hear her say "...Really? You lunkhead. Fine, I'll remind you." It is the best joke in the game and it teaches the whole system, so I keep taking the lesson.

Mark Right, Light does 6, Strong 36, and the blue marks climb with every hit. The boars shift stance on their own, and when they go nature they dig and heal 37. I keep chasing one boar down and it keeps coming back. That is the Burn plan from last time: fire on a nature boar, and if it burns it cannot heal.

Mark First real mistake. I got both of us up to 7 mana and lined Hina and Kailo up next to each other in the bar for a Combo, Pōhuehue, the fire and nature one. The vine game is a rhythm bar: notes slide onto a line and you press the key the narrator names, "up in 1.18s, tab in 1.58s". I got two of five. My presses land a little late, so I should send them a hair early. It still did 57. But the Combo ate every drop of both our mana and the boar healed 37 right back.

Mark And Hina is at 58 of 160 in nature stance, and the boars are in fire stance, and a fire hit on her is "Weak!" for 37 every time. She was in nature stance the whole fight. I said last time Hina should be in light near fire, and I did not do it. Hina is going down.

Mark The parry meter came up with Hina at 19. Three lanes, one for Light, one for Medium, one for Strong, and the buttons slide left toward a yellow zone. I parried the first Light dead center with "press c 3.09" and got "Parried!", and then I pressed the next one a tenth of a second late and got a "short metal clank". The narrator's times change after each press, so I should read the new time every single time. The next hit on Hina was 37 and Weak. "Hina falls."

Mark Kailo alone. 93 of 130. Two boars that heal 37 every cycle. I used all three Noni Pulu, each +30, and they are quick, you can use two in a row. I Sautéed the nature one for 24 and 26 Weak, but then they shifted to fire and it did 12 and 13, Resisted. I never saw a Burn. Three Sautés, no burn. I have no way to see their stance except guessing from the damage numbers after the fact.

Mark Nothing in Poi's menu either: Cook is gray, and the stir for it earlier also took two minutes to actually serve. 18 damage a hit, two boars. I parried two of three Medium and Strong blows twice, which saved me a lot, but one clank each time. At 1 HP I Defended, survived one round, Sautéed for 13 and then it just ended. Let me see what the screen says.

Mark And that is a Game Over. Kailo fell somewhere in my last two presses, in the opening tutorial fight, at about seventeen minutes in. So the very first fight of the game, the one that is supposed to teach me, ended in the black screen and the title. Nothing to continue, naturally, since there was never a save.

Mark Let me be honest about whose fault this is, because it is both of ours. What I did wrong: I spent both characters' mana on a Combo, I let Hina sit in nature stance while the boars were in fire stance, and I never saw a Burn. What the game did: it let me hit that spot with no warning at all, and it never once told me that stance decides who is weak to whom. Hina's own lesson about Nature burning easily is the only hint, and it is about the boars, not about her.

Mark So, New Game, and this time with a plan. I am answering Hina's question with Yes, "Do you remember how to fight", because I have taken the lesson twice and it forces me into odd turns. And I will watch whose stance is whose.

Mark "Good. Get ready." The free turns at the start are the best part of this fight. Kailo goes five times in the preemptive window, so Light, Medium, Strong for 6, 19 and 38, one more Light, and that is a boar nearly half gone before it has done anything. Then Hina three times in a row, and I notice her icon, the little sun, is the one lit. She is in light stance. When a boar finally hits her it says "Resisted", 11 and 9. That is the opposite of last time, when it was "Weak!" for 37 on her nature stance.

Mark So the first boar fell to Light, Medium, Strong and a Sauté. The second one gave me the same trouble as before. Anything fire I throw at it in its fire stance says "Resisted" for 12, 3, 2. Kailo's plain strokes are fire too. That matters: in this game your weapon strokes carry your stance, not just your Sauté. I did not know that before today. I Sautéed it again the moment it shifted to nature and got "Weak!" for 22.

Mark And three parries. A light at 3.03, a strong at 0.60 after that, another at 0.49. The trick is to read the numbers again after every single press, because the zone arrives at different times depending on what you did. With that, the boar's whole chain did nothing, and "Hina dodges Pua'a Hihiu B" on top of it. It feels very good when it works.

Mark Hina's Element is just Heal, and her Attack in nature stance against a nature boar says "Resisted" again, so I put a Strong on it the instant it was fire-weak and it fell. Victory at about twenty-four minutes. I got a Boar Hide, a Thorn Strike, and a Seer's Shell, no pule at all.

Mark After the fight Kailo feeds everyone and an Element slot unlocks, which I did not expect for a tutorial fight, and then the story beat I remember: one boar ran off, straight through the stew. Kailo, "...yeah, bruised taro still cooks. I just hate seeing the rest go to waste." Melia, "The Great Boar lives at the top of the woods... He sends the little ones down to steal taro for him, because he's too fat to come get it himself." Hina, "That is not how boars work." And Kailo's answer, "I'm going to go tell him to get his own taro." Hina goes home with "When you figure out you can't do this alone, you know where I live." I still love that. I am writing down: Great Boar at the top of the woods. Stew to remake. Wake before dark.

Mark Now look at this room. The grocer's stall on the left, the dug-up taro patch, the big hale on the right, and a carved winged figure standing up there next to it. I have seen that statue before and I always assumed it was one of Lanu's posts that wants a cup of water. This time I walked up to it and pressed z with nothing in my hands.

Mark "Every totem on the island listens. Tell the Akua what happened, and they remember it for you." And then "And they get anyone who's knocked out back on their feet." And then "The party kneels at the totem and tells the Akua all that has happened." And then, "Save your game?" Yes. Slot one, titled "The Pork Strikes Back". "Saved to slot 1."

Mark I have to stop and be loud about this. Four episodes. Four. I went through a whole game's worth of Game Overs because I did not know that the carved statues in the villages are save points. It is right there in the first town, forty steps from the start. I had decided they were something that needed water, because the one on the farm terraces and the one in the forest did. So the game has two kinds of post that look alike and do two different jobs, and nothing tells you. I am not going to say the game is hiding it, because the line "Every totem on the island listens" is a good line. But before it can matter you have to press z on a statue with nothing in your hand, and I never had a reason to try it empty-handed.

Mark Right. Saved at about twenty-seven minutes. From now on every post I meet gets a z, and the first time I am in trouble I know where I stand.

Mark Hina's house first. She is packing, "For my trip. I leave soon, and it's none of your business." Kailo is lost for words, which I like, and then "Did you forget what you were doing? You're hopeless, aren't you? Well, you need a healer anyway, so I'm coming too." And the pop-up says that while she is in the party the fallen get back up after a win. She is the priestess from the cards, and "headstrong" is right. I wrote down last time that her insults are how she cares, and this is the proof: she is leaving on a trip, and she is walking into a boar hunt because he cannot be trusted alone.

Mark A small thing on the map. I walked into the baskets outside the left house about four times. The fish and greens and tomato baskets block the way and the character just stands there. The narrator's directions sounded right and I still kept pressing left into baskets. A tiny thing, but it ate a minute.

Mark Kailo's House. Noelani is at the fire. "I heard what happened. The boars, the pot, all of it. I'll help you cook it. Don't make that face." And then the full list for the stew: "4 Fish, 3 Egg, 3 Coconut, 2 Pork, 2 'Uala, 2 Akai Lau, 1 'Awapuhi and 1 Māla Shoyu." "That's a lot. You fetch, I'll clean up this mess and get the fire going. Deal?" It is a scavenger hunt, and it gives me something clean to do besides the boar. And "I'll take my sandals off. ...wait we don't wear sandals." Funny, and it says Kailo talks before he thinks.

Mark Dad's chest. "My dad's chest." Found Eku. In the Equip screen the Eku says "Oar. Raises Vitality but lowers Agility." And the stat preview is the nice part: HP 130 goes to 160, Vitality 13 to 16, Strength 20 down to 16, Agility 16 to 13, Luck 8 up to 10, with red and yellow arrows. That is a proper gear screen, I can see the whole trade at once. I am taking the Eku. Kailo, the cook with a frying pan, picks up his father's fighting oar. Thirty more HP will have kept me alive in that tutorial, and a boar fight is a long one.

Mark Out into Kulāiwi Forest. The name banner, a lake with something green swimming in it, a pond, two roosters and a chest over on the right, boars wandering around under the trees, a chest and a red mushroom top left. I know this place. The short brown post by the pond is one of Lanu's: "A post for Lanu. I need a cup of water to leave her an offering." So that is the other kind of post, the one that wants water, and the carved totem in the village is the save. Two different things that look alike. I would give the save totems a different look, or at least a sign.

Mark Pressed z on the pond. "The party drinks from the cool pond. Everyone is rested." And both of us were at full health. That is a free heal I did not know about. I have been walking past ponds for four episodes, and last time I died at 4 HP three screens from one. I would not call that discoverable. It needs a line somewhere, in a sign or a villager. Writing it down: ponds heal.

Mark A boar got me while I was reading the pond text, so it was not a preemptive strike but an ambush, and the parry meter came up straight away. Tab at 3.26 parried, the second tab at 0.28 after that parried, and I tried to send the last two blows together, "press tab,z 0.28 0.09", and the second key clanked. Two keys at once works but the gap needs to be a hair smaller than the narrator's difference. Noted.

Mark And a surprise. With the Eku in my hands the second command is not Cook, it is Paddle. A mash minigame, mash A, 24 presses in about a second. It dodged twice, and then Kailo was "out of breath". And Sauté in the Element list is grayed out. I think the weapon decides which Skill and which element Kailo can use, which would be a really good idea if it were told to me. It was not. I walked into it. The fight won anyway: Light 6, Medium 16, Strong 36 and the boar fell. And one more observation: the blue marks went down while I attacked with the oar, 5, 3, 3, 0, the opposite of what they did with the frying pan.

Mark Two more roosters, a Red Feather and a Seed of Intelligence from the first one, only a Red Feather from the second, and a chest next to them with an 'Ōlena in it. No Egg from either, and Noelani asked for three. I tried to punch the palm tree for a coconut, since Tutori told me about punching trees with B for fruit. I pressed x and z facing it from right underneath and got nothing, at least four times. I do not know if I was facing it or if it needs something. I gave up on coconuts.

Mark I looked at Info while I was there. Info, Quests: "Open: The Great Boar, Stew for the wake." And the entry for the boar says "Melia told you the Great Boar is the king of the boars in the woods. He has to be beaten before the woods are safe again." So the log only repeats what I was told. It does not say where to go. The north of the forest is walled with orchard trees again, and I walked all the way round the lake to check, so it is not me being lazy. There is a gap at the top of the room and nothing I can do to get to it.

Mark The grocer, and I have nothing to buy with: 0 pule. Breadfruit 25, Flour 15, Noodles 30, Pia 15, Pineapple 25, Salt 5, and Akai Seed 25, Taro Seed 10, 'Uala Seed 25, Wheat Seed 10. Seeds for exactly two of the stew's ingredients, Akai Lau and 'Uala. So the stew list is built out of what the village can grow, and I would guess the game wants me to farm. But my earlier attempt to replant said "you're bad at gardening", so I need the gardening tool from somewhere, and I have no pule to buy seeds anyway. That is a chain of three things I do not have.

Mark The Chief's Hut, finally with time to read. Chief Ulu: "Aloha e Kailo. Bring your stew to Old Pono's wake tonight. He always said it was the best on the island." And: "And Hina leaves on her pilgrimage soon. Smart girl. She's earned the promotion." And "Ever since your dad left on his adventure, you've kept that whole house fed. We all noticed." So Hina is going on a pilgrimage, which is the "trip" she was packing for, and it comes with a promotion, so the Māla order is a real hierarchy. And Kailo's dad left on an adventure, and left the Eku in a chest. The Elder, "Pono and I fished the reef together for fifty years. Tonight we send him off properly." and "Your dad was the loudest man on this beach. You got his big heart, not his big voice." That is a good line about two people at once.

Mark Outside Pono's House, Nene. "Oh, Kailo. The house is so quiet with Pono gone. I haven't had a bite since he left." And then: "I could really go for some poi. Pono always said yours was the smoothest on the island." That is two small quests that fit together: the stew for the wake and the poi for a widow, and both come from the same grief. I would like to cook her the poi. I have two Taro.

Mark The farm terraces, north of Pono's House, past the big banyan. This is a pretty room. Six terraces of taro and wheat, a pond and a Lanu post in the top corner. I picked wheat and Hina showed up with "Don't leave it bare. It should be replanted. I'll show you how." and it takes a while to grow. I am enjoying how the plant growth is a clock, because "It is still growing." means I can come back. I did not have time to farm for pule, and I did not trust myself to leave the harbor errand for it.

Mark I walked west for the harbor, the whole way across the village in about eight commands. Some of that is the game's fault: after every room change my first walk command does nothing, and I stand there for a few seconds with the area sign still up. If I press x once, it works. It cost me a couple of minutes over the session and I would not have known to do it. Past the harbor, the west beach, banana trees, a sign, sea monsters and a chest on an islet. I recognize it. The chest is across water, and I told myself I need a way to fight down there.

Mark The Meialana, finally. A galley on a boat. Stove, chopping board with greens, a bowl, bananas, fish on the counter, a bed and a basket, and the sea through the window. It is the nicest room in the game so far. "What now? Cook / Check orders / Leave." Check orders says "No orders at the window." So the boat is a food stall, and I am guessing orders come in later.

Mark Cook. "Put up to three in to find a new recipe." I have Taro x2 and Wheat x1. The Poi recipe is already in the book, grayed out, and it says "Taro root pounded with water. Heals 40 HP." Pounded with water. I have no Fresh Water, so the recipe stays gray and I cannot cook Nene's poi. The game is telling me the missing ingredient in the description, which is good, and I did not notice until I read it twice.

Mark The pot toggles a unit each time I press z, which cost me a few tries. I put in just the Wheat and picked Cook: "Hm. That smells right. Let's see who eats it first." And the book gained a new line, "Toasted Wheat". So the recipe book fills in by trying things, which is the best part: discovery by playing. I would love for it to show what a recipe needs once I have found it.

Mark Ama's Bait & Tackle. He is a talker. "All my life on this water and she still surprises me. Flat as a mat at dawn, and by noon she wants your boat for kindling." "You learn her the way you learn a cousin." "A sailor's different. A sailor leaves. Every night out, you count the lights of the harbor behind you till you can't find them anymore." And then "Ama, I only came to say hello." "And I'm saying it! Hello! ...Where was I?" "The lights?" "The lights. Yes. Come and see me again, boy. There was something else, and it's out past the reef somewhere with my good sense." I wrote this down last time word for word: "something else, out past the reef." It is a thread dangling, and every episode it dangles again. It sounds like it ties to the mana line, "Moanaku out past the reef", and to Kailo's father being at sea. If I had to guess, it is going to be his father, and the Meialana is how Kailo sails out to find him.

Mark Then Ama's shop opens. Bait for 3 pule, "Draws more fish on the rod." Sell takes only my Taro, 4 each, and my bag reads Toasted Wheat, Taro x2, 'Ōlena, Thorn Strike x2, Seed of Intelligence, Boar Hide, Red Feather x2, Frying Pan, Seer's Shell. Bait means a rod, a rod means fish, and fish is the first thing on Noelani's list. I do not have a rod, no tool, and "Set to Y: no tool yet" is still on the map screen. So the game has a chain: tool, bait, pule, seeds, water. I can see the shape of it, and I did not reach the first link.

Mark Back across the village to the totem and I saved again. "Save over slot 1?" defaults to No, which I like, because an overwrite should be a bit hard. It works the way it should: slot 2, "The Pork Strikes Back", Kulāiwi Village, 0:17, Kailo and Hina's portraits. Seventeen minutes of play time, even though the session clock says fifty-six. So the in-game timer counts only active play and the studio clock counts everything I spent in menus.

Mark Last few minutes. I walked back to the forest to test one thing, whether I could get the Sauté back with the Eku in hand. I could not. The Element panel header says "Lelua" with the fire stance lit, and under it Sauté is gray. So the oar costs me my fire element. That is a real trade, and the stat preview did not tell me about it. The stat screen shows Vitality and Strength numbers and says nothing about what moves a weapon turns off. I would put it right under the stats: "Cannot use: Sauté."

Mark A boar fight to finish on. The Eku fight is a little slower, but the parries have been going well: Light at 3.04, then 0.62 for a Strong, then 0.49 for the last, three out of three, and another round of Medium, Medium, Strong with only the last one clanking. And at the end Kailo and Hina lined up side by side with full mana, so I ran the Pōhuehue Combo again, this time sending all five vine notes in one press with a 0.4 gap, "press up,tab,up,tab,z 1.14 0.4", and got "5 of 5". It hit the second boar for 61, and a message, "Pua'a Hihiu B curls up", and then "Sleep". So the vine puts the boar to sleep. That is the best use of a Combo I have seen. And it is also the first time a minigame rewarded me for planning the whole thing in one command instead of reacting to each beat.

Mark That is about an hour. I did not save at the end, because the totem is four rooms away from this forest and the clock was nearly up, but I did save twice earlier, with Hina in the party and the Eku equipped. Thank you for watching. Good place to stop. What I want to see next: the Great Boar, whatever it takes to get past the trees in that forest, a Fresh Water to cook Nene's poi, and what is out past the reef, because if Ama's something else is Kailo's father I want to know now.

End of episode

What happened

Route and events, in order.

1. Title screen, New Game. Four cards, then the opening in front of Kailo's and Hina's houses. Melia ran in about the boars. After the Melia scene Kailo and Hina walk to the taro room, a boar squeals, and the first fight starts automatically ("Preemptive strike!").

2. First game of the episode (nothing carried over from Episode 4). Answered No to Hina's "You do remember how to fight, right?" so the lessons ran. Two Pua'a Hihiu. Spent both characters' mana on the fire-and-nature Pōhuehue Combo (57 damage, a poor rhythm game), left Hina in nature stance, and she fell to Weak! fire hits of 37 at 19 HP. Kailo alone used all three Noni Pulu, never got a Burn from Sauté, and parried two of three blows twice. Game Over at 17:46. Nothing was saved.

3. Title again, New Game. This time answered Yes to Hina's question, which skipped the lessons. Hina's icon showed her in light stance this time, so boar fire hits on her read "Resisted". Beat boar A with Light, Medium, Strong, one Sauté and strokes; boar B with Sauté on its nature stance (Weak! 22) and a Strong from Hina (25). Parried a light, a strong and a strong in a row. Victory at 24:15. Drops: Boar Hide, Thorn Strike, Seer's Shell; 0 pule. An Element slot unlocked after the fight.

4. Cutscene: a boar ran through the stew, Melia's Great Boar story, Hina goes home. Used p ("Skip cutscene?") once by accident and said No.

5. In the grocer/taro room, pressed z on the carved totem with an empty hand: "Every totem on the island listens..." and "Save your game?" Saved to slot 1 at about 27 minutes ("The Pork Strikes Back", Kulāiwi Village, 0:04).

6. Picked two Taro, then found Hina at home ("For my trip... I'm coming too"). Hina joined.

7. Kailo's House: Noelani gave the stew list (4 Fish, 3 Egg, 3 Coconut, 2 Pork, 2 'Uala, 2 Akai Lau, 1 'Awapuhi, 1 Māla Shoyu). Opened Dad's chest: Eku. Equipped it (HP 130 to 160, Strength 20 to 16, Agility 16 to 13, Luck 8 to 10). Cook became Paddle, and Sauté is gray with the Eku.

8. Kulāiwi Forest (north of the start room). A Lanu post there ("I need a cup of water"). Pressed z on the pond: "The party drinks from the cool pond. Everyone is rested." (a full heal). One boar ambushed (parried two of three), won. Two Papanok: first by a map punch (32 damage) then Light, Medium, Strong; second by a preemptive fight. Drops: Thorn Strike, Red Feather x2, Seed of Intelligence. Chest by the roosters: 'Ōlena. The top-left chest, the red mushroom and the lake's north bank are still unreached; the orchard trees wall off the north exit again.

9. Info: Quests lists "The Great Boar" and "Stew for the wake". Timer 0:10 at that time, 122 steps, "30th of Kau".

10. Village: grocer shop (0 pule; seeds for Akai, Taro, 'Uala, Wheat). Chief's Hut (Chief Ulu, the Elder) and the Loft (empty baskets). Pono's House: Nene wants poi. Farm terraces: picked wheat, replanted with Hina.

11. Harbor: west beach (banana trees, sign, chest on an islet, sea monsters, not visited close), the Meialana (Cook: Poi is in the book but gray; discovered Toasted Wheat from one Wheat), Ama's Bait & Tackle (Bait 3 pule, sells only Taro).

12. Walked back to the totem and saved to slot 2 at 0:17 play time with Hina in the party.

13. Ended at 60:03 in a forest fight against two Pua'a Hihiu: boar A fell (Light/Dodge/Strong), the Combo put boar B to sleep (61 damage). Kailo 137/160, Hina 131/160. Not saved after that.

Fights won: 2 (opening tutorial), 1 forest boar, 2 Papanok, 1 boar (the last) with one more in progress. One Game Over.

Stuck and confusing

1. The first Game Over, in the opening fight. On screen: Hina at 19/160 after "37 Weak!" hits, Kailo at 1/130, parry meter up. Narrator said "Screen: game over" after my last z presses. The game had given no warning that Hina in nature stance was weak to fire and no way to see stances. I pressed z on Defend and attack many times; I never found an escape. Escape was gray the whole fight.

2. The stance swap. In battle, the menu's right page has Combo and Swap; Swap was gray. I pressed q and e (the L and R buttons) several times. The narrator never reports a change and the icons did not change. The Equip screen header shows L and R arrows, so I assumed they swap stance, but nothing happened. I still do not know how to change stance in battle.

3. The Config setting "Cursor: Reset" (each turn the command cursor starts on Attack) was not what I assumed, and I typed down, down at the wrong places four or five times; two of them used a Noni Pulu on a full-HP Kailo and one started a Cook stir by accident.

4. Cook was gray in battle (Poi grayed out) in game 1 late, and available in the opening of the same game; the game never says why. In game 2 Cook is replaced by Paddle when the Eku is equipped.

5. Sauté grayed out once the Eku was equipped (Element panel header "Lelua"; row "Sauté" gray). No message says why. I guessed the weapon gates the element.

6. After every change of room the first walk command does nothing; the narrator keeps saying "The last place sign read: ..." and the party stays put until I press x or walk again. Happened at least ten times.

7. Walking into baskets outside the left hale in the start room blocked me four times; the narrator reports the doors but not the baskets as obstacles.

8. Pressing x and z on a palm tree for a coconut did nothing, from directly underneath it. The Tutori hint said to punch trees with B.

9. The north gap in the forest room is visible but unreachable: orchard trees and the lake wall it off. The narrator lists "north (its nearest gap 6 left, 4 up)" with no path.

10. The cooking pot toggles one unit with z, and a second z on the same item removes it, so "Taro Taro" is hard to enter (the list says Taro x2 but the pot took only one). Poi is grayed out without telling me which ingredient is missing; the description says "pounded with water" but I have no Fresh Water and no way to get it.

11. Rhythm minigames: my presses land a little late if I send one at a time. I did not know that "press tab,z 0.35 0.08" would clank the second key when the gap was a hair too long.

12. The Lanu post says "I need a cup of water" and pond z gives a free heal instead of Fresh Water. I could not get a cup to make the offering.

13. No pule anywhere in this episode. The grocer sells things I cannot afford; nothing I fought dropped any.

14. Quest log gives no location for the Great Boar.

Design notes

1. The carved totem is a save point, and the game does not mark it as one (large). It sits next to the grocer in the first town and looks exactly like the Lanu posts, which want water and do something else. The text is lovely ("Every totem on the island listens. Tell the Akua what happened, and they remember it for you."), but I needed an hour and four episodes to press z on it empty-handed. A sign, a sparkle, or one line from Tutori would fix it. This also explains four Game Overs.

2. Stance, weakness and resistance are the core of the fight, but the screen never shows them (large). The enemy's stance, and mine, are only learned by the word "Weak!" or "Resisted" after a hit. A small icon over each boar would turn guessing into planning. In the opening fight it cost me the game.

3. Free healing at ponds is a big discovery and unmentioned (medium). "The party drinks from the cool pond. Everyone is rested." resets HP, which makes the whole forest much less punishing. It needs to be told once.

4. Parry feels good once the numbers are read again after every press (medium, praise). The narrator times shift after each parry, so reading them again is what works; a string of three parries in a row with a multi-key press feels like earning it. Sending several keys in one press with a gap works for blocks and for the vine rhythm minigame (5 of 5).

5. The tutorial fight is lost on a bad stance, and nothing tells you to set Hina's stance before it (large). The correct state, Hina in light stance, was set by default this time, and the fight went smoothly; the first time, an identical fight against the same boars ended in a Game Over. The difference is hidden.

6. Equipment is a real trade-off screen (medium, praise). The Eku shows green and red arrows on every stat before you equip it. But it also silently swaps Cook for Paddle and disables Sauté, and that is not in the preview (medium). Show the changed Skill and Element names in the preview.

7. The Combo is excellent and gets better in the second playthrough (praise, medium). Pōhuehue's vine put the boar to sleep and did 61 damage. Lining Kailo and Hina up with full mana is a good puzzle; Defend and Light strokes slide you into place.

8. The recipe book fills in by experiment (praise, small). One Wheat gave "Toasted Wheat" with the line "Hm. That smells right. Let's see who eats it first." Gray recipes show their text ("Taro root pounded with water. Heals 40 HP."), which tells you what is missing, but only if you read.

9. Cursor memory on the battle menu is configurable, and the default makes the menu feel random (small). "Each turn, the battle commands start on Attack" is in Config. With Paddle gray, "down" from Attack skips to Element, which also changes the number of presses needed.

10. The "first walk after a room change does nothing" bug (medium). It looks like a stuck input and ate a lot of the session.

11. No pule from monsters in the forest and a shop I cannot afford. The farm-and-sell loop is the only income, and nothing says so (medium).

12. Writing is the strongest part again (praise, medium): Hina's "Don't make it weird", Chief Ulu's "She's earned the promotion", Ama's "A sailor leaves", the Elder's "You got his big heart, not his big voice". The island gets a history from small lines.

13. The first walk to the north gap in the forest is walled by trees again; the Great Boar is not reachable (large, still). The quest log's text says only what Melia said.

14. The Meialana kitchen is a lovely room, and "Check orders: No orders at the window." makes me want to know when there will be some (small).

15. Minigame inconsistency: Paddle's mash dodged twice and left me "out of breath" with no explanation. What "out of breath" does is unclear (medium).

Story and characters

Story so far, with what this session added. Kulāiwi Village, last day of Summer. The boars ruin the stew for Old Pono's wake. Melia says the Great Boar lives at the top of the woods and sends the little ones for taro; Hina says "That is not how boars work." Kailo decides to tell the boss boar to get his own taro. Hina goes home to pack for a pilgrimage ("For my trip"), then joins anyway. Chief Ulu says Hina leaves on her pilgrimage and has "earned the promotion", which makes her trip an assignment from her order. Kailo's father left on an adventure and left a Kame fighting oar, the Eku. Ama: "A sailor leaves... There was something else, and it's out past the reef."

- Kailo: warm, quick to speak and slow to think ("I'll take my sandals off. ...wait we don't wear sandals."), proud of his stew, takes up his father's oar.

- Hina: sharp, insults as care ("Did you forget what you were doing? You're hopeless, aren't you?"), priestess of the Māla order, on a pilgrimage; best lines in the game.

- Melia: Kailo's younger sister, loud, with a sling; her Great Boar story is a child's telling that may be accurate.

- Noelani: runs the household, "Don't make that face," "Don't track mud in"; I think she is their mother.

- Chief Ulu: calm, knows everyone's business; the Elder: fished with Pono fifty years, remembers Kailo's dad as "the loudest man on this beach."

- Nene: Pono's widow, wants poi.

- Ama: harbor man, drifts mid-sentence; his unfinished "something else" is a hook.

- Old Pono: still never seen; his wake ties the quests together.

Predictions

Open: Hina is the devout priestess on the cards (nearly right, since Chief Ulu says she leaves on a pilgrimage with a promotion); Kailo's dad left on a sea voyage and Ama's "something else, out past the reef" is about him; the Meialana carries the party off Māla Iki after the wake; somebody in the south takes mana from beaten champions; the Great Boar is in the north woods and needs a tool or route I have not found; trees wall the north exits until a tool is found (an axe, probably from the hunters' lodge, which I have not found); Noelani is Kailo and Melia's mother; the chests across water open once the party can fight in water; the north-beach birds are not wind or spirit; the grove's stall may be the lodge; the five Lanu posts matter later.

Right: the carved totems matter (the first one I tried, the one in the taro room, saved my game and healed the party). The Eku would be Kailo's father's, and Chief Ulu confirmed the father "left on his adventure". Hina in light stance resists the boars' fire ("Resisted" 11 and 9). The boar chain can be parried at three out of three with the multi-key press. Boars are weak to fire in nature stance (Weak! 22 and 25 with Sauté).

Wrong (this session): I expected Hina to be fine in nature stance in the opening fight (she fell). I expected the Eku to be a pure upgrade (it removed Sauté and Cook). I expected a pond to give Fresh Water (it healed instead).

The booklet

Never opened. No emergency came up: every confusing thing was worked out from the screen, even if it cost me time.

Review so far

This is a game that wants to be a Chrono Cross-style RPG with a cooking island at the center, and the most original part is the way a fight is a clock: heavier moves push you further down the turn bar, you parry with your own buttons, and two friends lined up side by side with full mana can run a Combo that is its own minigame. When it works it is wonderful: a three-for-three parry and a vine that puts a boar to sleep is as good as anything in the genre. The writing is warm and specific, the island feels lived in, and Hina is the best character I have met in a game this year.

What does not work is information. The game hides everything that decides a fight: whose stance is whose, what is weak to what, which weapon turns off which move, that ponds heal and totems save. All of it can be found by trying, but a Game Over wipes the only thing you have, and the first one arrives in the very first fight. Once I found the totem and the pond, the game turned from punishing to pleasant. I would not recommend it today to most players, only to patient ones who like to experiment; with a marked save point, a stance icon on each enemy and a line about ponds it would be an easy recommendation.

My notes for next time

Mark's notebook, written for himself.

*What is saved.* Two saves: slot 1 "The Pork Strikes Back" at 0:04 (taro room, before Hina joined) and slot 2 at 0:17 (Hina in the party, Eku equipped). Continue works now. The last fight is not saved. Kailo 137/160, Hina 131/160 at the end, in a forest fight with one boar asleep.

*The big rules, so I stop dying.*

- The carved winged totem in the taro room (east of the start room, near the grocer) is a save point and revives the fallen. Every totem on the island does it. Lanu's posts are the short brown L-shaped ones and want a cup of water.

- Ponds heal the whole party: face the pond and press z.

- Answer Yes to Hina's "do you remember how to fight" to skip the slow tutorial; check Hina's icon is the sun (light stance) so fire hits on her read "Resisted".

- Weakness shows only as "Weak!" or "Resisted" after a hit. Boars flip stance every turn or two; Sauté (20% burn) is good only when the boar is in nature. Burn never landed this session.

- With the Eku: more HP, no Sauté, Paddle instead of Cook (mash z, 24 presses). If I want Sauté, go back to the Frying Pan.

- Parry: read the narrator's times again after every press. If two blows are close, send both keys in one press: "press tab,z 0.35 0.08" (gap a hair smaller than the narrator's difference).

- The vine Combo: "press up,tab,up,tab,z 1.14 0.4" got 5 of 5 and put the boar to sleep.

- After each room change the first walk does nothing; walk again.

*People and what they told me.* Chief Ulu: "Hina leaves on her pilgrimage soon. Smart girl. She's earned the promotion." "Ever since your dad left on his adventure, you've kept that whole house fed." The Elder: "Pono and I fished the reef together for fifty years. Tonight we send him off properly." "Your dad was the loudest man on this beach. You got his big heart, not his big voice." Nene: "I haven't had a bite since he left." "I could really go for some poi. Pono always said yours was the smoothest on the island." Ama: "A sailor leaves." "There was something else, and it's out past the reef somewhere with my good sense." Noelani's stew list: 4 Fish, 3 Egg, 3 Coconut, 2 Pork, 2 'Uala, 2 Akai Lau, 1 'Awapuhi and 1 Māla Shoyu. Melia: the Great Boar lives at the top of the woods and sends the little ones.

*Places.* Kulāiwi Village runs west to east: harbor (west, Ama's, the Meialana, then the west beach), start room (Hina's House east door, Kailo's House west door), the taro/grocer/totem room with the Chief's Hut (and Loft), the east room with Pono's House and the banyan, the farm terraces north of it (taro, wheat, a pond and a Lanu post). Forest north of the start room (boars, Papanok, pond, post, chest 'Ōlena taken, top-left chest and mushroom not taken, north gap walled by trees).

*Things for sale and tools.* Grocer: Breadfruit 25, Flour 15, Noodles 30, Pia 15, Pineapple 25, Salt 5, Akai Seed 25, Taro Seed 10, 'Uala Seed 25, Wheat Seed 10. Ama: Bait 3. Sells only Taro (4). I need pule. The Y tool slot is empty.

*What to do next.* Find a way to get Fresh Water (cook Nene's poi), a cup for Lanu's post, a tool for the trees (maybe a lodge axe), and pule from the farm (Taro and Wheat sell for 4). Try the orchard north of the taro room again and the unreached east chests. Look for the lodge. Keep Kailo on the frying pan when I need Sauté, on the Eku when I need HP. Check Hina's stance before every hard fight. And find out what is out past the reef.
